question: How the bayonet clamp spreads with its interference tolerance and temperature, and the collar wall its lug load then needs — the number of the conditional root-package member (02_02 §4.4).
form: PEEK-dominated loop (k = k_PEEK): cap_needed(k) = L0/f + k·[2δ + Δα·L·((ΔT_c + (1 − f)·ΔT_h)/f + ΔT_h)]; a series spring makes f_eff = f/(f + φ(1 − f)), φ = k/k_PEEK, so the load runs continuously to the force-controlled L0 (plus k_s·spread)
assumptions: the loop at the capsule's temperature — NOT conservative; the gradient-bound reading takes α_PEEK alone
relaxation acts on the mechanical clamp; the summer thermal increment relaxes too before the winter (one summer)
L0 at the band's top with the ring never relaxing; the ring's force in the cold is taken, not bounded
lug-root capacity linear in the wall (73, pure shear — collar bending under eccentric lugs would lower it)

inputs.hot_edge_reading: 71: lumped capsule mean, sunlit, still air, h_c × 0.7, absorptance 0.50 (canon finish)
inputs.delta_from: ±interference tolerance; 0.05 = the class the shop is asked for the groove depth (52 DEPTH_TOL_ASKED) on one Z dimension, 0.10 = both at it; neither is specified
inputs.span_from: radome.json lock_groove_z_mm − (lug_radius_mm + slot_clearance_mm); lock_groove_z is a placeholder (HW.8)

peek_column.is: the loop's stiffness if a PEEK annulus over the span were its ONLY compliance — not what sits under the lugs (the load enters through three line contacts), so a ceiling and no estimate of k

missing_data: k: the lug contacts, the ledge, the lug's, collar's, flange disc's and boss ring's bending (FEA or bench; lug geometry placeholder, HW.8)
δ: the tolerances of the lock-groove Z and the lug Z (neither specified)
the ledge's local creep under contact stress above the PEEK yield
the PEEK at the sunlit base vs the lumped capsule mean; the ring's force below room temperature; resin swell (88)
the PEEK's share of the loop compliance (it sets how much of f applies)
a compliant element's force tolerance and space, if the clamp is made force-controlled
verdict: A deflection-controlled clamp moves with its interference tolerance and with temperature through the loop stiffness k. In a PEEK-dominated loop (k = k_PEEK, the PEEK relaxing by f — the form `52` and the member assume) every N/µm adds 0.049 mm of wall at the window top with a ±0.05 mm interference over the capsule requirement (temperature 11 % of it), 0.0055 mm with no tolerance (0.0067 with a Ti–PEEK gradient) — so such a loop needs more than the ratified 0.28 mm for any k, which is its lower bound, not an estimate. A compliant element in series makes the relaxation and the k-terms fade, and the lug load runs continuously down to L0 — 411 N at the window top, a 0.18 mm wall with a zero force band — so the ratified number is one point on a curve of an unmeasured k, bounding nothing. That force-controlled end is not cheap: to stay inside the print floor its spring must be no stiffer than 0.42 N/µm with ±0.05 mm and zero force tolerance (≈ 1.0 mm of working deflection), its whole force band fits ±5.3 %, and a soft clamp gives the rim almost no stiffness against tipping. Separately, the lug is a radial pin on a flat ledge — a line contact — whose peak pressure at the window top is 320–397 MPa (174–215 at the window floor; 258–320 at the window top even under the force-controlled L0) against 167 MPa for first yield of the PEEK at its tensile yield (the compressive yield is higher and not in the tree): the ledge yields and creeps beyond `52`'s f across the window under the PEEK-dominated load, and at the window top under either clamp. With ±0.05 the print floor carries a PEEK-dominated loop at the window floor up to k = 2.41 N/µm and at the nominal up to 1.05. k, δ and the PEEK's share of the compliance are not computed — the lug geometry and both Z tolerances are placeholders; the member goes back to the founder (02_02 §4.4).
